content.title: Subsurface Trace to Breach | Scale Reversal and Residual Aftermath
content.summary: Establish adults and stable route landmarks at ordinary scale, then escalate one directional subsurface trace through two visible ground states. The same trace becomes the breach point for an original large entity, whose scale and route remain measurable before the moving agents exit and a changed environment holds as aftermath.

quick_start.input_format: at least one clearly adult moving subject and three stable route landmarks establish ordinary scale + one subsurface trace moves directionally through at least two ground-state escalations + trace, breach point and subject stay in one geography + original large entity fully appears and uses adults plus landmarks for scale proof + entity crosses or pursues along the established route without teleporting + damaged surface, suspended material and original landmarks remain in a held aftermath
quick_start.recommended_input: Two adult salt-flat surveyors follow three sensor stakes while a crystal ridge escalates underfoot, an original segmented mineral glider breaches and follows the same stake route, then broken salt and suspended teal dust remain after all moving agents leave the foreground.
required_anchors: Establish at least one clearly adult moving subject and three stable route landmarks before the ground anomaly begins.
Move one subsurface trace in a readable direction and escalate it through at least two ground states before emergence.
Use the adult and at least two established landmarks to prove scale while the entity crosses or pursues along the same route.
After the moving agents exit, hold persistent displaced material and the original landmarks.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Establish adults and stable route landmarks at ordinary scale, then escalate one directional subsurface trace through two visible ground states. The same trace becomes the breach point for an original large entity, whose scale and route remain measurable before the moving agents exit and a changed environment holds as aftermath.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Establish at least one original clearly adult moving subject inside an ordinary route with three stable scale landmarks. Introduce one attributable subsurface trace that travels in a readable direction relative to the subject and escalates through at least two observable ground states before any body is visible. Keep the trace, breach point and subject in one geography when an original large entity emerges; hold them together long enough to prove scale, then let the entity cross or pursue along the established route without teleportation. End after the moving agents leave the immediate frame and hold on persistent dust, displaced material or broken surface plus the original landmarks. The reusable mechanism is ordinary scale baseline, directional hidden warning, staged ground escalation, same-space breach, landmark-based scale proof and aftermath hold—not the source adults, faces, clothing, giant ant, rural road, tanks, desert, genre or decade reference, exact actions, camera shake, creator identity or timing.

invariants.rule: Establish at least one clearly adult moving subject and three stable route landmarks before the ground anomaly begins.
invariants.purpose: Creates a human-scale baseline and recoverable geography for the later breach.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without ordinary landmarks, the entity's size and continuity cannot be verified.

invariants.rule: Move one subsurface trace in a readable direction and escalate it through at least two ground states before emergence.
invariants.purpose: Builds warning and causality from hidden motion instead of a surprise cut.
invariants.ablation_failure: An instant creature appearance removes the trace-to-breach mechanism.

invariants.rule: Keep subject, trace and breach point in one geography when the original large entity emerges.
invariants.purpose: Proves that the visible body is the cause of the prior ground disturbance.
invariants.ablation_failure: A cut to a separate creature shot can imply an unrelated event.

invariants.rule: Use the adult and at least two established landmarks to prove scale while the entity crosses or pursues along the same route.
invariants.purpose: Makes the scale reversal measurable and keeps action spatially continuous.
invariants.ablation_failure: A tight monster close-up may look large without demonstrating its relation to the route.

invariants.rule: After the moving agents exit, hold persistent displaced material and the original landmarks.
invariants.purpose: Shows that the breach materially changed the established world.
invariants.ablation_failure: Resetting to a clean road erases the consequence and weakens closure.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source adult runners, faces, bodies, beige clothing, footwear and exact panic performance
the source giant ant, insect anatomy, mandibles, legs, abdomen and attack behavior
the source dry rural road, drainage channel, utility poles, sheds, cylindrical tanks and desert palette
the source genre and decade references, named film-style comparison and creature wording
the source pursuit choreography, camera shake, framing, creator identity, Seedance 2.0 post wording and 10-second timing
